reason: While the passage shows Moses expressing initial concern for his people's welfare and burdens (v. 11), his subsequent actions contradict the principle of responsibility and accountability. Moses kills the Egyptian and conceals the body in sand rather than taking open responsibility (v. 12). When he later attempts to intervene in a dispute between Hebrews, the challenged man questions his authority: 'Who made you a ruler and judge over us?' (v. 14), indicating Moses lacks legitimate leadership standing. Critically, Moses does not accept accountability—he becomes afraid when the deed is discovered and flees Egypt entirely (v. 14-15) rather than facing consequences. The passage presents these actions as generating problems rather than exemplifying good leadership; Pharaoh himself becomes the enforcer of accountability by seeking Moses' death. The text does not position this as a model of responsible leadership but rather as unauthorized action with unfavorable outcomes.
